title: Geometry-Informed Neural Operator for Large-Scale 3D PDEs
layout_note: two rows: a block schematic on top (input, GNO, FNO, GNO, prediction) and, below, the same pipeline drawn on a rendered car (mesh, point cloud, latent lattice, Fourier layers, lattice, point cloud, coloured prediction), the columns roughly aligned
grouping: No containers: the top row of boxes is the abstract pipeline with a one-line role under each operator ('Operates on input geometry', 'Operates on (latent) regular geometry', 'Projects to output geometry'); the bottom row is the concrete instance, placed under the matching boxes.
shapes_depth: Top row: flat rounded rectangles in saturated green with dark-green outlines for the operators, sharp-cornered grey boxes with white text for input and prediction. Bottom row: shaded 3-D render of a car mesh, green point-cloud cars, green wireframe cube lattices with black nodes, a translucent red ball, a small rounded box of stacked sine waves for the Fourier layers, and a final point-cloud car coloured by a colour map.
proposed_highlight: All three operators are the same saturated green boxes against grey input/output boxes; the bottom row shows what each operator does to the geometry, with a red ball marking the neighbourhood that links points to one lattice node.
lesson: Put an abstract block row directly above the same pipeline drawn on one concrete instance, so each block's label sits over the geometry it produces.
notes: The arXiv first page prints no venue, so venue = arXiv and year = arXiv preprint year (2309.00583); remembered venue NeurIPS 2023, not confirmed. Domain given as scientific-ml in the candidate list; the knowledge base's id for that area is ai4science. The crop has no colour key for the output car's colour map.

arrangement.units: two unframed rows separated by whitespace: a block schematic on top and the rendered car pipeline below
arrangement.inputs_as: a grey 'Input Samples' box on top; a shaded 3-D car mesh below
arrangement.shared: the two GNO boxes are identical green boxes, and the two lattices below them are drawn the same way

taxonomy.task: surrogate prediction of 3-D PDE solutions (surface pressure) on varying irregular geometries

insights.structure: Two aligned rows, abstract blocks on top and the same pipeline on a rendered car below, so the schematic and the instance explain each other.
insights.data: The input is a shaded car mesh, intermediates are green point clouds and wireframe lattices, and the output is the point-cloud car coloured by predicted values.
insights.emphasis: The operators are the only saturated-colour boxes; the red ball is the one accent and marks the graph neighbourhood that maps points to a lattice node and back.
insights.flow: Both rows read left to right on straight grey arrows; red and grey dashed lines between ball and lattice show the geometry-to-grid and grid-to-geometry maps.
insights.avoid: Green fills the operator boxes and also colours the mesh, points and lattices, and the output colour map has no key.

core.what: the operator chain drawn on one car: mesh to point cloud, a red neighbourhood ball mapping points onto a latent lattice, Fourier layers on the lattice, and a ball mapping back to points

relations.form: the bottom row renders each stage on the car: points, lattice, lattice, points, with a red ball and dashed lines showing the neighbourhood that links points and one lattice node
Input Samples, GNO, FNO, GNO, Prediction on one horizontal line with 'discretize' and 'query' labels on the end arrows
the top block row is placed over the bottom rendered row column by column, each block's role written under it, so a block and its geometry share a column

channels.colour: green = the method's operators in the top row and also the geometry rendering (mesh, points, lattices) in the bottom row; grey = input and output boxes; red = the neighbourhood ball; output car colour = predicted values (unkeyed)
channels.shape: rounded box = learned operator, sharp-cornered box = data endpoint, lattice cube = latent regular grid, point-cloud car = irregular geometry, stacked sine waves = Fourier layers
channels.line: solid grey arrows = flow; red dashed = points-to-lattice neighbourhood; grey dashed = lattice-to-points query
channels.frame: none; the only rounded frame encloses the Fourier-layer glyph

quality.strengths: The method is drawn on a small instance of its structure, as derive.md asks: the irregular point cloud, the regular latent lattice and the neighbourhood ball that maps between them are visible as geometry; the abstract row sits over the concrete row so labels need not be repeated; every arrow is straight and left to right; the operators are the only saturated boxes.
quality.weaknesses: Green carries both 'learned operator' and 'geometry'; the output colour map is unkeyed; the two rows are only roughly column-aligned (the second GNO box sits to the right of the second lattice it acts on); grey input/output boxes with white text are low-contrast; the SDF features the caption says are concatenated before FNO are not drawn.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)
